Competing in the sphereX challenge

Strong passion for software and web development
summary: Welkin is an interactive map meant for data analysis using the SphereX viewer. It creates an accessible option for the general public to explore complex NASA data without extensive technical knowledge, while simultaneously serving as a powerful tool for data analysis and research. As a student myself, I realized that Welkin has strong potential to enhance learning experiences and satisfy curiosity. Knowing the application must feel approachable and easy to use for students to learn, I focused on these aspects. As a result, Welkin puts an emphasis on both powerful features and UI/UX in order to appeal to less experienced users while also having complex research capabilities. Welkin addresses the challenge by serving as a public-facing, web-based tool in order to view the SphereX data published by NASA that simplifies the process of making new astronomical discoveries; users will enter the coordinates of a patch of sky (right ascension and declination), and then Welkin will display a series of frames to help visualize, as well as give users the option to analyze the object's motion graph. Overall, Welkin provides a user-focused approach to allow people of all backgrounds to interact with the data.
details: Welkin, named for the old English word for sky, is a public web application built for the SphereX challenge that turns complex NASA astronomical data into an interactive, easy-to-navigate sky map. Users enter right ascension and declination coordinates or search by object name to explore celestial movement over time through an interpolated frame player, pixel-by-pixel difference modalities, 102-band infrared spectra, and a 3D motion viewer that graphs paths and exports datasets to Excel. Welkin was built with React, Vite, Aladin Lite v3, and WebGL2 on the frontend alongside a Python, Flask, Astropy, Astroquery, and NumPy backend. It also integrates IRSA archives with SIMBAD and VizieR catalogues. Its creative strength is in bridging advanced research tools with an approachable interface that uses gold and purple contrast overlays, motion-aware right-click identification, and shareable state URLs so anyone can participate in scientific discovery. When developing Welkin, I prioritized balancing computational power and intuitive UI/UX design, ensuring all backgrounds can easily understand the data without sacrificing analytical aspects for experienced researchers. Overall, Welkin makes real-time infrared sky data accessible, visual, and collaborative for anyone interested in learning using the app.
